correctness.rationale: For f(0)=0,f(1)=01,f(2)=011 and required ternary prefix 0121012, consider all preimages u for which f(u) is palindromically rich and avoids every exponent >=14/5. Both properties are hereditary under taking prefixes: forbidden powers persist and palindromic defect is nondecreasing under appending a letter. Every extension therefore belongs to a finite prefix tree whose root is 0121012 and alphabet branches 0,1,2, and pruning never removes a valid descendant. Independently written incremental palindrome-suffix and forbidden new-suffix tests produced level survivor counts n=47:11,48:6,49:3,50:0, proving the maximum 49 and the exact three stated words with common 47-letter prefix. Independent final full palindrome-factor and period tests found binary image lengths 94,95,96, all rich, with critical exponents 46/17,46/17,95/34 (each <14/5). The complete level-by-level enumeration through 50, not an arbitrary cutoff or timeout, certifies the exhaustiveness, subject to the elementary hereditary proof.
